title: Why You Can't Tickle Yourself (Your Brain Predicts the Touch)
description:
You can't tickle yourself because your cerebellum predicts the touch from your own movement and cancels the response; a stranger's touch, or a delayed one, isn't predicted, so it still tickles.

The tickle meter levels and the cancelling waveforms are illustrative, not measured data. The hand and feather art is a simplified cartoon.

Narration is a synthetic voice (VoiceStudio). Animation is written as code.

#Shorts #Neuroscience #Brain
